title: Crew Cascade and Clarity Huddle
summary: Leadership gave a compact update on Q4 priorities (reliability, Dedicated ramp, Private deployments), reviewed an incident postmortem action tracker, and set cross-functional next steps for a 6-week delivery window. Ops and People noted hiring and onboarding targets; product called out a small scope shift for inference cost controls. Several questions about SLAs and region rollouts; follow-ups assigned.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (CEO), Maya (CTO), Jordan (VP Product), Priya (Head Eng), Sam (Head People), plus functional leads on the line

[00:00] Sam: okay, thanks everyone for joining, we'll kick off in one minute, check audio, check video.
[00:18] Alex: cool thanks Sam, yeah good to see folks. Quick agenda: one, quick reliability postmortem highlight, two, product & infra priorities for the next 6 weeks, three, people/hiring notes, and Q&A. Try to keep it tight.
[00:33] Maya: yeah, I'll start on the postmortem. As you saw in the doc, last week's KV cache eviction cascade had two triggers, an unbounded prefix size from a rolling experiment plus a kernel-level mem spike on one instance. We fixed it with a targeted patch and restarted the affected nodes.
[01:02] Priya: to add, the hotfix reduced tail latency by 40% on the affected pool but we observed slower recovery in the secondary region due to a stale autoscale policy that didn't trigger soon enough. Not ideal.
[01:25] Jordan: question — did the canary signal get suppressed because the ratio threshold was set too high?
[01:32] Maya: yeah it was conservatively tuned, and there's some metric aliasing coming from the old tracer. We're going to remove the alias and lower the threshold so the canary is more sensitive.
[01:50] Alex: okay thanks, high level: we need both short-term stopgaps and a slightly larger effort to prevent recurrence. Priya, what's your ETA for the autoscale policy change?
[02:03] Priya: We can push the policy change by EOW, plus an infra job to verify it across regions early next week.
[02:12] Sam: note for people — there were some CX tickets and a handful of customers pinging about errors; Diego and CS handled comms, thank you.
[02:24] Alex: big thanks to CS. Moving on: Jordan, product priorities — lay out the 6-week plan please.
[02:33] Jordan: Sure. Top three: one, make Optimize cost-controls GA internal (batching suggestions and quantization recommendations), two, Harden Dedicated autoscale and burst policies for guaranteed throughput SLA, three, Complete Private deployment doc set for EU data residency pilot. There's a small scope shift: we'll postpone the large model-variant rerouting feature in favor of shoring up the quantization profiles — it's cheaper immediate ROI.
[03:02] Maya: on Dedicated autoscale we need tighter SLOs for burst scenarios and a fallback to lower-cost variants when GPU contention is detected. That's the smart routing tradeoff we discussed previously.
[03:18] Alex: tradeoff acknowledged; product you own the customer impact comms, infra owns the fallback mechanics.
[03:26] [03:30] (crosstalk) Priya: also note the Private on-prem package has an extra compliance checklist — KMS integration and audit-logging which we must validate with the security team before the EU pilot.
[03:44] Jordan: yep, security review scheduled with OpsSec Thursday.
[03:50] Alex: Hiring — Sam?
[03:53] Sam: We're prioritizing three SRE hires and two infra engineers; goal is to have offers out in two weeks. Onboarding plan updated, we'll pair SRE candidates with a 2-week immersion in the runtime stack.
[04:12] Priya: can we make sure the SRE hiring scorecard includes experience with kernel-level perf debugging and batching systems? We saw that gap.
[04:21] Sam: added.
[04:24] [04:30] Alex: cool. Quick financials — Laura sent a short update: Q3 beat plan on revenue; margin compressions are driven by higher burst usage and more long context runs. Jordan, any product levers for noisy tenant isolation?
[04:49] Jordan: yes, we'll push tenant-level soft limits and improved batching heuristics to reduce tail costs; the Optimize tool will surface tenant suggestions. Expect a performance experiment week starting Oct 18.
[05:05] Alex: good. We got a few questions in the chat about SLOs and region coverage — Maya, can we answer high-level?
[05:13] Maya: high-level: we plan to add another EU region before year-end, and a Singapore region in H1 next year pending provider availability. SLA tiers: hosted will keep a 99.9 latency SLO for standard models, dedicated will get a contractual throughput SLA (details in the draft contract).
[05:34] Alex: people will want a written summar y — Jordan please include the SLA table in the 6-week plan doc.
[05:40] Jordan: will do.
[05:42] [05:50] Priya: about security/compliance, OpsSec flagged a gap in audit retention for Private on-prem installs. We need a design to ensure append-only logs and a recommended retention policy — opssec wants it by the EU pilot kickoff.
[06:06] Maya: I'll coordinate with security.
[06:10] Alex: great. Open Q&A — notable items: Marco asked about pricing for Dedicated burst; Laura asked about the runway for extra capacity; Marco's question: will burst pricing be usage-based or fixed bucket? Jordan: leaning usage-based with cap controls. We need finance sign-off.
[06:36] Sam: there's some filler — I'll summarize the ask in follow-ups.
[06:45] [06:50] (noise) Alex: all right, rapid-fire updates from each function — 90 seconds each. Priya?
[06:58] Priya: infra will ship the autoscale policy and hotfix, start the region verification job, and pair SRE hires with kernel-debugging rotations.
[07:13] Maya: runtime improvements — KV cache eviction fix in prod, kernel guardrails for mem spikes, and a perf tracing rollout to reduce metric aliasing.
[07:28] Jordan: product — Optimize cost-controls reprioritized, Dedicated autoscale SLA doc, Private EU checklist complete draft. Also, will host a customer webinar for Dedicated in mid-Nov.
[07:44] Sam: People — hiring timeline, updated scorecards, ramp plan for new hires, and a new internal onboarding repository. Also, review of interview loops.
[07:58] Alex: closing thoughts — focus on delivering the 6-week plan, be explicit about who owns comms, and keep everyone accountable. We'll reconvene biweekly to track progress.
[08:12] (multiple people): thanks, good meeting, bye

Notes and imperfections: transcript has occasional misheard words (e.g., "KV cache eviction cascade" transcribed sometimes as "KV cash eviction"), speaker labels changed mid-sentence at times, timestamps approximate. References shared: doc: https://redwood.internal/6-week-plan (internal), postmortem: https://redwood.internal/postmortem/kv-2026-10-01, SLA draft: https://redwood.internal/legal/sla-draft.
